text: What does cannabis do to my brain?

args.label: Cannabis (example, smoked)

targets.effect: Binds CB1 receptors: high, slower memory, altered timing
Speeds heart rate for an hour or two
Soaks up THC and releases it slowly for days

args.source: Huestis 2007, Chem Biodivers: smoked THC peaks in plasma within ~3-10 min, bioavailability 10-35%, Vd ~3.4 L/kg; 2 h approximates the effect-phase decline, not the multi-day terminal phase.

args.label: Cannabis high (example)
args.source: Own estimate guided by Huestis 2007 and Jones 2002: heart rate up ~20 bpm peaking within 30 min of smoking, appetite up, drowsiness afterwards.

feelings.label: High
feelings.cause: THC holding CB1 receptors in the brain

stops.label: Inhaled
stops.say: THC crosses the air sacs into blood within seconds of each puff.

stops.label: Brain
stops.say: It reaches the brain and grips CB1 receptors on nerve endings.

stops.label: Heart
stops.say: Heart rate climbs as blood vessels widen.

steps.title: An example puff
steps.say: As an example, say you smoked a joint now. THC crosses the air sacs into your blood within seconds, so it reaches your brain in minutes.

composed.caption: THC crossing from air sac into blood
composed.basis: Huestis 2007: smoked THC reaches peak blood levels within minutes

steps.title: THC finds CB1 seats
steps.say: Your brain has its own cannabis-like messengers that act as a brake on busy nerve endings. THC sits on those same CB1 seats and pushes the brake down everywhere at once.

composed.caption: THC braking a nerve ending
composed.basis: Textbook endocannabinoid signalling: CB1 receptors on presynaptic terminals reduce transmitter release

steps.title: Why it feels that way
steps.say: CB1 is densest in memory, timing, coordination and reward areas. So short-term memory slips, minutes stretch, movements get clumsier, and released dopamine makes things feel pleasant or funny.

composed.caption: Reward nerves release more dopamine
composed.basis: Bossong et al. 2009 (PET): THC modestly raises striatal dopamine; CB1 maps from Herkenham 1990

steps.title: Your heart speeds up
steps.say: THC also widens blood vessels and the heart answers by beating faster. In this example your heart goes from about 78 to about 98 beats a minute, which a watch would show.

steps.title: Fading, but not gone
steps.say: By around 23:40 the high has mostly faded and you may feel sleepy. THC dissolves into fat, which leaks it back out slowly for days, so tests find it long after.

composed.caption: Fat soaking up THC, releasing it slowly
composed.basis: Huestis 2007: THC is highly fat-soluble, with a terminal half-life of days in regular users

lines.text: THC presses your brain's own braking system, mostly in areas for memory, timing and reward.
You may feel memory slip, time stretch, clumsiness, and a dopamine lift that makes things fun.
In this example, your heart rises from about 78 to 98 beats. Tonight's beer adds impairment.
